summary.title: How to Write a Postmortem
summary.one_liner: Learn why and how Server Density writes incident postmortems: their purpose, timing, content, and who is responsible for writing and publishing them.
takeaways: Postmortems help teams refocus after an outage by forcing a pause to reflect on what happened and what to change.
Publishing detailed postmortems to customers rebuilds credibility and rewards transparency and over-communication during incidents.
Postmortems are drafted internally (in Jira) first, taking about a week after resolution to confirm the fix and gather input from all teams and providers.
A good postmortem covers the root cause, detection and isolation steps, affected services, the fix, and lessons learned.
Whoever leads incident response or is on call posts status updates and drafts the postmortem, which is reviewed by the team before the CEO publishes it.
summary.summary: This 2016 blog post by David Mytton of Server Density explains the company's approach to postmortems after service outages. It argues that postmortems help teams return to important work, rebuild customer trust through transparency, and capture lessons from failure. The article describes the workflow: short status page updates during an incident, a roughly one-week gap to verify the fix and align internal and external parties, then a drafted postmortem reviewed internally before public release. It closes with a suggested content outline (root cause, investigation, impact, fix, learnings) and who is responsible for each step.
